title: Streaming stutter detection and continuity recovery playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a capacity pressure event on 2026-03-09 we observed a class of streaming failures that manifests as short "stutter" bursts (clients receive duplicated offsets, truncated tokens, or repeated partial-frames) and intermittent silent pauses before reconnect. Affected tenants experienced incomplete responses and elevated reconnect rates. Root-cause signals point to a combination of (1) worker-level write stalls when kernel scheduling thrash coincided with large batch spikes and (2) client-facing backpressure semantics that do not preserve sequence continuity across reconnects. This ticket captures the detection rules, immediate mitigations, and a concrete set of follow-up engineering tasks to eliminate recurrence.
timeline:
2026-03-09 10:12 UTC: First alert - streaming p50 latency spike on region us-west-2.
2026-03-09 10:18 UTC: Support reports increased reconnect rate from a high-volume customer.
2026-03-09 10:32 UTC: Oncall traces show repeated "stutter" windows (0.5-2s) where tokens are duplicated or truncated; KV cache offsets misaligned in ~30% of traces.
2026-03-09 11:05 UTC: Rolling scale-up and emergency throttling reduced error surface; customer mitigation applied (route to dedicated pool).
2026-03-09 14:00 UTC: Post-incident telemetry collection and initial triage completed.
2026-03-10 to 2026-03-13: Investigation and prototype detection rules developed.
decisions: 1) Ship an ops playbook and detection alert before code changes. 2) Implement sequence fencing + per-stream checksums in the runtime (short-term checksum header) to detect truncated/duplicated frames. 3) Rework backpressure signals to be explicit (PAUSE/RESUME tokens) rather than relying on transport-level stalls. 4) Prioritize kernel-scheduling fixes in runtime-1.23; defer KV cache structural changes to runtime-1.24. 5) Establish canary rollout for any change touching streaming continuity with a 1% traffic gate and automated rollback on increased reconnects.
action_items: AI-1: Add "stutter" detection alert (SLO-guard) that fires on repeated partial-token signatures in a single session — owner: Liam O'Connor — due: 2026-03-15
AI-2: Prototype short-lived per-stream checksum header in serving protocol; implement proof-of-concept in branch feat/stream-checksum — owner: Priya Desai — due: 2026-03-20
AI-3: Update backpressure semantics to include explicit PAUSE/RESUME frames and a client behavioral doc — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2026-03-24
AI-4: Instrument KV cache offset sanity checks and emit 'offset-mismatch' event with sample payloads — owner: Chen Wei — due: 2026-03-18
AI-5: Add e2e test in the streaming-test-harness that simulates kernel scheduling stalls and validates continuity under reconnects — owner: Liam O'Connor — due: 2026-03-22
AI-6: Run capacity stress test with multi-tenant burst patterns and observe stutter regression after kernel patches — owner: Performance Team (rollup) — due: 2026-04-01
AI-7: Customer communication: send a concise incident summary and planned mitigation timeline to impacted customers — owner: Sarah Patel (Support) — due: 2026-03-16
acceptance_criteria: 1) New 'stutter' alert fires with test vectors in staging and has <2m mean time to detect in canary traffic.
2) Per-stream checksum proof-of-concept prevents at least 95% of observed truncated-frame cases in stress replay tests.
3) Explicit PAUSE/RESUME flow-control reduces reconnects caused by transport stalls by >=80% in synthetic tests.
4) No increase in overall token latency beyond 5% in canary population after runtime-1.23 patches.
5) Post-release: <0.1% streaming sessions show continuity anomalies over a 30-day window for canary customers.
